sections.heading: Understand the organization before choosing a target
paragraphs: Agriculture, Food and Forestry employers can differ in how they organize production linked to land, biological cycles, processing, and supply relationships. While reading a role description, compare its named responsibilities with the candidate's experience of resource planning, safety-minded operations, supplier relationships, yield or quality context, and continuity decisions; then ask how those duties connect to seasonality, input availability, quality variation, and coordination across production stages. This keeps a sector label from standing in for an employer's actual mandate.

Use understand the organization before choosing a target to examine the particular organization, not an assumed industry template. In Agriculture, Food and Forestry, producers, workforce, buyers, processors, logistics partners, and communities may have different relationships from one employer to another. A candidate can ask how production linked to land, biological cycles, processing, and supply relationships is defined, who owns the relevant decisions, and what evidence of resource planning, safety-minded operations, supplier relationships, yield or quality context, and continuity decisions is appropriate to discuss.
